nodes.label: Accept Interfaces, Return Structs
nodes.rationale: Functions accept interface parameters for flexibility and testability but return concrete types so implementation details are not hidden unnecessarily.

nodes.label: TDD RED-GREEN-REFACTOR Cycle
nodes.rationale: Write a failing test first, implement minimally, then refactor with tests green; tests double as documentation of intended usage.

nodes.label: Sermo Variable Expansion (${var} and built-ins)
nodes.rationale: Simple string variables plus built-ins (${name}, ${display_name}, ${arch}, ${os}, ${service}, ${host}) and runtime values (${date}, ${event}, ${action}); nested variables are rejected and unresolved variables fail validation. Typed fields (port, expect_status) use tolerant FlexInt scalars parsed after expansion so quoting or ${var} never breaks YAML.

nodes.label: Metric Scope (service vs system)
nodes.rationale: Metric checks carry scope: service (default, this service's process set/cgroup) or system (whole machine). Safety: remediation rules may only trigger on service-scope metrics; a system-scope metric may drive alert only, never an operation action on a single service.

nodes.label: Named Runtime Locks (<paths.runtime>/locks)
nodes.rationale: Named runtime locks derive from <paths.runtime>/locks and internal operation locks from <paths.runtime>/ops; paths.locks and /etc/sermo/locks.d are not supported so active locks are never loaded from config directories. file_exists checks must not point under the locks dir — the engine checks Sermo locks itself.

nodes.label: Library Restart-on-Change (restart_on_change.libraries)
nodes.rationale: A service opts into library-change restarts; this desugars at resolution into one remediation rule per library using the changed condition (size/mtime differs from across-cycle baseline; first cycle adopts, successful restart re-baselines). Referenced names must be library catalog documents.

nodes.label: Injectable Command Runner (internal/execx)
nodes.rationale: Never call os/exec directly from many packages: route every external command through an injectable Runner interface (Run(ctx, name, args...) returning stdout/stderr/exit code/duration) so every command is context-bounded, timeout-bounded and testable with fake runners.

nodes.label: Sermo internal/ Package Layout
nodes.rationale: Canonical internal/ package map (app, checks, cli, config, execx, locks, operation, process, rules, servicemgr, state, web, ...) that skills and tests must match exactly — do not invent or drop packages; Linux-specific behavior stays behind interfaces.

nodes.label: servicemgr Manager Interface
nodes.rationale: Common interface (Backend, IsAvailable, Status, IsActive, Start, Stop, Restart) so systemd and OpenRC differences stay isolated behind one abstraction.

nodes.label: Init Backend Autodetection
nodes.rationale: Detection must not rely only on command existence: systemd needs /run/systemd/system (degraded is still usable), OpenRC needs /run/openrc or rc-status fallback; when both are present prefer the init system actually active.

nodes.label: stop_policy.kill_only_if
nodes.rationale: force_kill: true is rejected unless paired with a restrictive kill_only_if clause (users + exe_any); a residual killable only when EVERY field matches exactly. SIGKILL requires explicit permission and this clause.

nodes.label: Sermo (safe service monitoring and control system for Linux)
nodes.norm_label: sermo (safe service monitoring and control system for linux)

nodes.label: Shared Safe Operation Engine
nodes.rationale: Daemon and CLI must both use the same config resolver, servicemgr.Manager, rule engine, guard evaluator, lock manager, safe operation engine and process discovery; safety checks live in the operation path, not in callers, so sermod never calls systemctl/rc-service directly and sermoctl cannot bypass guards.

nodes.label: First-Four Gate (staged mutating fleet runs)
nodes.rationale: Any mutating fleet action runs end-to-end on only the first four usable .env.ssh hosts first; the rest proceed only when every first-stage outcome is success or a documented host-local skip, so a Sermo blocker (reproducible project/catalog/deployment bug) never spreads to the whole fleet. Read-only collection is exempt.

nodes.label: Dry-Run Alert / Notification Safety
nodes.rationale: Remote tests must never execute then.hook or alter server behavior: verify alert routing with alert-only watches or target-level dry_run: true plus a notify selection — dry run logs/events what would happen and skips hook, expand, kill and non-wall notify delivery.

nodes.label: Run-Time Host-Watch Inventory
nodes.rationale: Complete remote installs build a fresh host-watch inventory from the exact local checkout being deployed (watch builder, checks builder/type registry, validation, docs) instead of a static list, with an availability gate: generate a watch only with positive read-only evidence that its kernel interface/device/daemon/tool exists; otherwise record the skip reason.

nodes.label: Rule Windows (for = consecutive, within = rolling)
nodes.rationale: for.cycles means consecutive matches; within.cycles + min_matches is a rolling window. A rule cannot define both — validation rejects ambiguous windows; mode belongs only to defaults.rule_window.

nodes.label: Guard Rules (type: guard, blocks + block action)
nodes.rationale: Guards block listed operations (e.g. restart/stop during backup) and must be evaluated before remediation; block and alert actions require a message and only guard rules use action: block.
nodes.norm_label: guard rules (type: guard, blocks + block action)

nodes.label: Per-Service Remediation Policy (cooldown / max_actions / backoff)
nodes.rationale: Cooldown and rate limiting are a per-service policy block (mandatory positive cooldown), NOT per-rule; the daemon checks it before invoking the operation engine so restart loops are prevented while rules may keep firing. Manual sermoctl actions are exempt from cooldown but still pass guards, locks and preflight. Window state (for/within history) is separate per-rule state.

nodes.label: golangci-lint v2 Configuration
nodes.rationale: Runs gosec plus focused bug analyzers not covered by standalone tools (gofmt, staticcheck, revive, govulncheck cover the rest). G115 accepted project-wide because flagged conversions are already bounded; by-design exceptions are suppressed inline with justification rather than widening the config.

nodes.label: Depguard Architecture Import Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Safety invariant enforcement via lint: read-only layers (internal/checks, internal/conn, internal/rules, internal/config) must not import the operation engine — checks are read-only predicates, protocol probes must not dispatch service operations, rule conditions must not run commands (no execx in rules); service control goes only through app/operation.

nodes.label: markdownlint Configuration
nodes.rationale: Focused only on structural Markdown issues that break rendered docs; broader prose/style checks deliberately belong to a separate pass.

nodes.label: yamllint Configuration
nodes.rationale: Extends default with 220-char lines, 2-space indentation and consistent indent-sequences, mirroring .yamlfmt so catalog/example YAML has one canonical formatting.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md — Sermo Project Conventions
nodes.rationale: Describes only current behavior and invariants; planned features live in TODO.md so missing items are not treated as accidental gaps.

nodes.label: AI Agent Standard Git Workflow
nodes.rationale: Agents use the same normal Git workflow as humans in the current checkout to keep one visible source of truth, avoid hidden integration queues, and preserve unrelated user edits; commit/merge only when explicitly requested.

nodes.label: Validation Gate (make check)
nodes.rationale: make check is the single command covering vet, full tests, lint (fmt-check, go fix -diff, staticcheck, revive, golangci-lint, govulncheck), scripts-lint, yaml-validate, markdown-check and web-check. Bare go test/go vet is insufficient because it skips checks that catch issues the Go toolchain does not.

nodes.label: Reuse and Shared Behavior Principle
nodes.rationale: Default to the smallest change preserving current design: reuse existing owner > extend owner > small private helper > new package, in that order. Never duplicate validation/parsing/comparison/notification/dispatch logic across sermod, sermoctl, web, watches and services. Treat a user example as evidence of a use case across equivalent surfaces, not the full scope.

nodes.label: Protocol Probe Interface Binding (SO_BINDTODEVICE)
nodes.rationale: Every internal/conn probe must honor cfg.Interface through BindDialer/BindListenConfig so probes egress a specific link on multi-homed hosts. Interface binding wins over code reduction: codec-only libraries are preferred, libraries accepting a custom dialer are acceptable, libraries that dial internally are rejected (why the DHCP probe keeps its own raw-socket transport).

nodes.label: Security and Safety Invariants
nodes.rationale: 16 non-negotiable invariants: never kill by name only; no SIGKILL without explicit policy plus kill_only_if; process matching requires exact resolved exe + user; guards and preflight block actions; mandatory positive policy.cooldown prevents restart loops; every action/block is logged; atomic TTL-bounded locks with PID-reuse-safe stale reclaim; one independent worker per service so a long operation never blocks other monitoring; remediation triggers on service-scoped metrics only.

nodes.label: Configuration Structure Changes — Break by Default
nodes.rationale: Public config changes break compatibility by default with one canonical spelling; no dual parsers, aliases or migration shims. Valid exceptions: Linux/init compat (/var/run normalized to /run), hard safety invariants, and catalog sugar (reload_on_change/restart_on_change) that desugars one-way during resolution in internal/config/resolve.go.
nodes.norm_label: configuration structure changes — break by default

nodes.label: README.md — Sermo Overview
nodes.rationale: Sermo is a portable service supervisor over systemd and OpenRC: validates services before acting, detects blocking operational state, discovers real processes, and applies guarded remediation — never restarting blindly. sermod runs as root because it manages services owned by different users and needs privileged access; config is therefore trusted root-owned input and /etc/sermo must stay root-only.

nodes.label: sermoctl (Operator CLI)
nodes.rationale: Operator CLI: status, safe start/stop/restart/reload/resume, config validate, locks, processes, preflight, per-service availability/SLA. Read-only commands do not need root.

nodes.label: sermod (Monitoring Daemon)
nodes.rationale: Daemon with one independent worker per service running checks, evaluating rules and driving remediation through the same safe operation engine sermoctl uses; also runs host watches, notifications (email, Slack, Teams) and an optional loopback web dashboard to be exposed only behind a TLS reverse proxy.

nodes.label: Sermo Web Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Loopback HTTP dashboard (web.port, recommended 9797) with per-service checks, SLA history, latency graphs and an event feed; optional auth, TLS via reverse proxy only.

nodes.label: TODO.md — Future Improvements
nodes.rationale: Future work moved out of AGENTS.md so instructions describe only what exists: cluster mode, remote agents, RBAC, plugin ABI, metrics export, service priorities, exec rule action, tree-scoped process watches; tracks catalog preflight config coverage and completed observability integrations (Prometheus, Alloy, Loki, InfluxDB, Grafana).

nodes.label: Certbot

nodes.label: Cockpit
nodes.rationale: Web-based Linux admin console. Both 'binary' (cockpit-tls) and 'bridge' (cockpit-bridge) variables are path lists to cover distro layout differences (/usr/libexec vs /usr/lib/cockpit vs /usr/bin). Version is read from cockpit-bridge because cockpit-tls does not expose '--version'; health uses cockpit-tls '--help'.

nodes.label: containerd
nodes.rationale: Also checks containerd-shim-runc-v2 as an optional secondary binary, since the shim may not be installed on all hosts; category virtualization.

nodes.label: CUPS
nodes.rationale: Health check runs 'cupsd -t' (config syntax test). Version comes from the separate optional cups-config helper binary because cupsd itself has no version flag; both cups-config checks are optional.

nodes.label: Berkeley DB (db%v)
nodes.rationale: Oracle Berkeley DB utilities. Uses versioned app-name template 'db%v' with ${version} interpolated into the binary name (${bindir}/db${version}), so one entry matches db5, db18, etc.; version probe uses '-V'.

nodes.label: D-Bus
nodes.rationale: System message bus daemon (dbus-daemon binary); category system; standard binary + '--version' preflight pattern.

nodes.label: Versioned App Name Template (%v)
nodes.rationale: Catalog convention where an app name contains '%v' and ${version} is substituted into binary paths, letting a single catalog entry describe every installed version of a runtime (Erlang BEAM erts dirs, Berkeley DB db${version} binaries).

nodes.label: Device-mapper event daemon (dmeventd)
nodes.rationale: Included in the catalog because it monitors and auto-repairs DM devices (mirrors, snapshots, thin pools), making it a system-critical storage daemon

nodes.label: Docker Engine
nodes.rationale: Defines three binaries (docker CLI, dockerd daemon, docker-proxy) with the proxy resolved via a multi-path fallback list and marked optional, because docker-proxy location varies across distributions and may be absent

nodes.label: Dovecot
nodes.rationale: Enumerates seven helper worker binaries (anvil, log, config, stats, auth, imap-login, imap) each with libexec/lib/lib64 fallback paths and optional flags, so the daemon's per-process monitoring works across distro layouts without failing preflight when a worker is not installed

nodes.label: EPMD (Erlang Port Mapper Daemon)
nodes.rationale: Has no own version command, so it declares version_from: erlang to inherit the Erlang/OTP runtime version; its health probe accepts exit codes 0 or 1 because 'epmd -help' exits non-zero on some versions

nodes.label: etcd
nodes.rationale: Companion tools etcdctl and etcdutl are optional preflight probes so the app validates on hosts that only install the server binary

nodes.label: Fcron
nodes.rationale: Uses a hardcoded /usr/libexec/fcron path instead of ${bindir} because fcron installs outside standard bin directories

nodes.label: FireHOL
nodes.rationale: Version probe runs the bare binary with expect_exit: 1 because firehol exits 1 when invoked without arguments while still printing identifying output

nodes.label: firewalld
nodes.rationale: Version is read via firewall-offline-cmd --version rather than the daemon or firewall-cmd, so preflight works without a running daemon or D-Bus session

nodes.label: version_from Inheritance Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Lets an app without its own version flag inherit the reported version of another catalog app, avoiding duplicated or fake version probes

nodes.label: Multi-path Binary Fallback Resolution
nodes.rationale: A variable may hold a list of candidate paths; the first existing path wins, so one catalog entry covers libexec/lib/lib64/bin layout differences across distributions

nodes.label: expect_exit Non-zero Exit Tolerance
nodes.rationale: Command preflight checks can declare acceptable non-zero exit codes for tools whose version/help invocations do not exit 0

nodes.label: irqbalance
nodes.rationale: Version preflight uses expect_exit: 1 because irqbalance --version exits non-zero; the catalog schema supports overriding the expected exit code per command check.

nodes.label: Java Runtime (JVM)
nodes.rationale: Declared as an instanced/versioned app template (name: java-%i-%v) because multiple JVM vendors and versions coexist; the binary is resolved from a candidate list of common /usr/lib/jvm layouts and the current default version is detected from the /usr/bin/java symlink (versions.current_from).

nodes.label: Apache Kafka
nodes.rationale: Kafka ships as JVM shell launchers; the runtime itself is owned by the java app and linked from each kafka service, so the app definition only proves the distribution is installed and reports its version via kafka-topics.sh --version (the canonical way without a running broker). The install dir is repeated in both binary and topics paths because catalog variables are flat — a value cannot reference another variable — so both must be overridden to relocate the distribution.

nodes.label: libvirt D-Bus
nodes.rationale: Uses a --help health command instead of a version check, since libvirt-dbus exposes no version flag.

nodes.label: listmonk
nodes.rationale: listmonk is a single self-contained binary whose path is deployment-specific (often under the app's web root), so the binary variable is expected to be overridden per install.

nodes.label: MariaDB
nodes.rationale: Binary candidates cover both mariadbd and legacy mysqld names, and version_match requires the string 'MariaDB' to avoid matching an Oracle MySQL binary installed at the same path; the client binary is optional since only the server is monitored.

nodes.label: Instanced/Versioned App Template (%i/%v)
nodes.rationale: Catalog mechanism where an app name contains %i (instance) and %v (version) placeholders, binary is a list of candidate paths tried in order, and versions.current_from resolves the system-default version from a symlink — lets one definition cover many coexisting JVM installs.

nodes.label: Libraries Preflight Check
nodes.rationale: Preflight check type 'libraries' that inspects a binary's shared-library dependencies; optional for HAProxy but mandatory for MariaDB, reflecting how critical dynamic linkage health is per app.

nodes.label: Eclipse Mosquitto
nodes.rationale: mosquitto has no --version flag, so the version preflight runs '-h' whose usage output begins with 'mosquitto version 2.0.22'.

nodes.label: MySQL (mysqld)
nodes.rationale: Defines both server binary (mysqld) and optional client binary (mysql); adds a libraries preflight check on the server binary.

nodes.label: MySQL version_match excludes MariaDB
nodes.rationale: version_match: { excludes: MariaDB } prevents a MariaDB build (which also ships a 'mysqld' binary and prints MariaDB in --version output) from being identified as MySQL.

nodes.label: BIND (named)
nodes.rationale: Requires the named-checkconf helper binary as a mandatory preflight in addition to the daemon binary, enabling config validation.

nodes.label: NetworkManager
nodes.rationale: nmcli helper binary is declared as an optional preflight check, so absence of the CLI does not fail app detection.

nodes.label: version_from Mechanism (nfsdcld -> rpc-mountd)
nodes.rationale: nfsdcld exposes no usable version flag, so the catalog delegates version detection to the rpc-mountd app definition via 'version_from: rpc-mountd'; both binaries ship in the same nfs-utils package so their versions match.

nodes.label: Samba NMB (nmbd)
nodes.rationale: Requires smbcontrol and testparm helper binaries as preflight checks; testparm is given as a candidate path list (/usr/bin, /usr/sbin) to handle distro packaging differences.

nodes.label: Node.js
nodes.rationale: Declares two version preflights: '-v' for the standard tagged version and '-p process.versions.node' for a short bare version string.

nodes.label: OpenSSL
nodes.description: Full-strength general purpose cryptography library (including SSL and TLS)

nodes.label: Patroni
nodes.notes: binary variable is a fallback list: ${bindir}/patroni, /bin/patroni

nodes.label: Performance Co-Pilot
nodes.notes: Version source app for the PCP daemon family via version_from

nodes.label: PHP-FPM (versioned)
nodes.notes: Multi-version app template: name php-fpm%v, binary ${bindir}/php-fpm${version}; optional libraries preflight

nodes.label: PHP (versioned)
nodes.notes: Multi-version app template: name php%v, binary ${bindir}/php${version}

nodes.label: PCP Collector (pmcd)
nodes.rationale: pmcd ships under PCP's libexec tree, not ${bindir}; binary and PMDA agent paths are fallback lists across /usr/lib, /usr/libexec, /usr/lib64 and /var/lib/pcp because distributions place them differently. PMDA checks are optional so absence does not fail preflight.
nodes.notes: version_from: pcp; checks optional PMDA agents (root, proc, xfs, linux, kvm)

nodes.label: PCP Inference Engine
nodes.notes: version_from: pcp; health check accepts exit codes 0 and 1 (expect_exit)

nodes.label: PCP Inference Engine Farm
nodes.notes: version_from: pcp; libexec fallback path list; optional pmpause helper binary

nodes.label: PCP Archive Logger
nodes.notes: version_from: pcp; health check accepts exit codes 0 and 1

nodes.label: PCP Archive Logger Farm
nodes.notes: version_from: pcp; libexec fallback path list; optional pmpause and pmsleep helper binaries

nodes.label: Polkit
nodes.notes: Daemon binary at /usr/lib/polkit-1/polkitd; version obtained from pkexec --version since polkitd has no version flag

nodes.label: PostgreSQL (versioned)
nodes.notes: Multi-version app template: name postgres-%v, binary /usr/lib64/postgresql-${version}/bin/postgres

nodes.label: Python (versioned)
nodes.notes: Multi-version app template using %n placeholder: name python%n, binary ${bindir}/python${n}; version_short via platform.python_version()

nodes.label: version_from Inheritance
nodes.rationale: PCP sub-daemons (pmcd, pmie, pmlogger and their farm variants) declare version_from: pcp so their reported version is inherited from the parent pcp package instead of probing each helper binary, which mostly lack usable version flags (health uses -? with expect_exit [0,1]).

nodes.label: RabbitMQ
nodes.rationale: Preflight verifies both the server binary and rabbitmqctl; version is obtained via rabbitmqctl rather than the server binary itself.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.rationale: Adds a libraries preflight check on the server binary to detect broken shared-library links, unlike most sibling app definitions.

nodes.label: NFS idmapd
nodes.rationale: rpc.idmapd has no version flag, so it delegates version reporting to rpc-mountd via version_from and uses a -h health probe instead.

nodes.label: RPC Bind
nodes.rationale: rpcbind exposes no version command, so version_from delegates to rpc-mountd; preflight only checks binary presence.

nodes.label: Rspamd
nodes.rationale: Preflight checks the auxiliary rspamadm admin binary in addition to the main daemon.

nodes.label: Rsyslog
nodes.rationale: Uses an absolute binary path with a per-OS override block: Gentoo installs rsyslogd under /usr/bin instead of /usr/sbin, demonstrating the catalog's os-specific variables mechanism.

nodes.label: OS-Specific Variable Override
nodes.rationale: Catalog mechanism allowing an app definition to override variables per operating system (os: gentoo: variables: ...) so one definition covers distro layout differences.

nodes.label: Ruby
nodes.rationale: Provides both a full --version check and a version_short check via inline eval (print RUBY_VERSION) for a machine-parsable version string.

nodes.label: S-nail
nodes.rationale: Binary variable is a fallback list (s-nail or mailx) because distros install the mailx-compatible client under either name; also runs a config parse check with a longer 30s timeout.

nodes.label: OpenLDAP (slapd)
nodes.rationale: Version check declares expect_exit: 1 because slapd -VVV prints its version but exits nonzero by design; binary and slaptest variables are multi-path fallback lists covering distro-specific install locations including /usr/bin/openldap.

nodes.label: SNMP UPS Driver
nodes.rationale: NUT drivers live under distro-dependent lib directories, so the binary variable is a four-entry fallback list across /usr/lib64, /lib64, /usr/lib and /lib nut subdirectories.

nodes.label: Squid
nodes.rationale: Declares optional helper binaries (pinger, log_file_daemon, security_file_certgen) with multi-path fallbacks because Squid helper locations vary across distros (libexec vs lib vs lib64 vs squid3) and helpers may not be installed.

nodes.label: systemd
nodes.rationale: App identity is anchored on systemctl rather than the PID-1 binary, since systemctl is the stable client interface for verifying presence and version.

nodes.label: Apache Tomcat (versioned template)
nodes.rationale: Uses name 'tomcat-%v' and ${version} in the binary path so multiple parallel Tomcat major versions installed under /usr/share/tomcat-<v> can each be modeled as a distinct app instance.

nodes.label: UPower (upowerd + upower client)
nodes.rationale: Splits daemon (upowerd, no version flag, probed via --help) from CLI client (upower --version, optional) because the daemon binary itself does not expose a version command.

nodes.label: libvirt Network Daemon (virtnetworkd)
nodes.rationale: Declares dnsmasq as an optional preflight binary because libvirt NAT networks rely on dnsmasq for DHCP/DNS, but virtnetworkd itself can run without it.

nodes.label: Multi-Path Binary Fallback
nodes.rationale: A variable may list several candidate absolute paths; preflight resolves the first that exists. Trade-off: verbose catalog entries in exchange for one definition working across distro filesystem layouts (Debian, RHEL, lib64, libexec).

nodes.label: Optional Preflight Check
nodes.rationale: Checks marked optional: true do not fail app detection when the binary/command is absent, letting the catalog document helper components without making them mandatory.

nodes.label: Health Probe via --help
nodes.rationale: Daemons that expose no version flag (udisksd, upowerd) are health-checked by running the binary with --help, which exits successfully and proves the binary is executable without starting the service.

nodes.label: Versioned App Template (%v / ${version})
nodes.rationale: App name contains %v and paths interpolate ${version}, so one catalog file instantiates per-version app entities (e.g. tomcat-9, tomcat-10) instead of duplicating definitions.

nodes.label: Web Server Configtest Signals Pattern
nodes.rationale: Shared analyze pattern so nginx/apache configtest output is classified uniformly: [emerg]/syntax error/test failed as errors, deprecated/[warn] as warnings.

nodes.label: Grafana Alloy Service
nodes.rationale: Preflight runs 'alloy validate --stability.level=<level> <config>' before restart so a broken config never takes down the telemetry collector; health is probed via /-/ready and /metrics HTTP endpoints.

nodes.label: Apache HTTP Server Service
nodes.rationale: Preflight 'apachectl -t' output is analyzed with the shared web pattern; stop_policy kill_only_if restricts force-kill to processes owned by www-data/root running the apache binary to avoid killing unrelated processes; remediation policy uses cooldown 15m, max 2 actions/hour with backoff.

nodes.label: Asterisk PBX Service
nodes.rationale: Monitored via dedicated 'asterisk' check type against the AMI port 5038 in addition to plain TCP; sustained single-thread CPU above 90% for 6m triggers restart.

nodes.label: atftp TFTP Server Service
nodes.rationale: Uses a protocol-aware 'tftp' check on UDP port 69 instead of a TCP probe because TFTP is UDP-only.

nodes.label: Automount Service
nodes.rationale: Covers both autofs and automount unit names across systemd and OpenRC; health verified with a dedicated 'autofs' check type.

nodes.label: Avahi Service
nodes.rationale: mDNS/zeroconf health probed via dedicated 'avahi' check type rather than a port probe.

nodes.label: Backrest Service
nodes.rationale: Web UI/orchestrator for restic backups; HTTP check accepts any status < 500 since the UI may redirect or require auth.

nodes.label: Bacula Director Service
nodes.rationale: Preflight 'bacula-dir -t' config test guards restarts; monitored on director port 9101.

nodes.label: Bitbucket Pipelines Runner Service
nodes.rationale: No apps: reference and no restart_on_change — the self-hosted runner is deployed out of band, so only service state and resource metrics (memory %, fds) are watched.

nodes.label: Ceph Metadata Server Service
nodes.rationale: MDS binds dynamic ports in the 6800-7300 range assigned at startup, so it is monitored by service state, process presence, and the admin-socket 'status' command instead of a fixed port probe; uses templated unit ceph-mds@${hostname}.

nodes.label: Ceph Manager Service
nodes.rationale: Hosts cluster management modules (dashboard, prometheus, balancer); health via admin-socket 'status' command analyzed with the ceph pattern, restart after 3 failed cycles.

nodes.label: Ceph Monitor Service
nodes.rationale: A mon binds its msgr v2 port (3300) to the cluster/public network address rather than loopback, so the TCP and ceph-protocol probes against ${host}=127.0.0.1 are optional and off by default; the admin-socket mon_status command is the authoritative health signal. Set 'host' to the mon's bind address per instance to enable active probing.

nodes.label: Ceph OSD
nodes.rationale: Ceph OSDs bind dynamic ports in the 6800-7300 range across public and cluster networks, so health is monitored by systemd service state and admin-socket status commands rather than a fixed port check. Templated per backing device via ceph-osd@${n}.

nodes.label: ClamAV Daemon
nodes.rationale: The clamd protocol check on the LocalSocket is optional because the socket path is deployment-specific; a socket-path mismatch must not flip an active clamd to failed. Service state plus pidfile are the authoritative liveness signals.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Tunnel
nodes.rationale: Preflight validates tunnel ingress config only when the config file exists, so hosts without /etc/cloudflared/config.yml can still start. Uses a dedicated cloudflared protocol check against the local metrics endpoint plus a stop_policy kill guard restricted to the cloudflared user/binary.

nodes.label: Cockpit
nodes.rationale: Socket-activated web console: also_service tracks cockpit.socket, and the session/wsinstance sockets are optional since they only exist while sessions are active.

nodes.label: containerd
nodes.rationale: Container runtime underlying Docker/Kubernetes. restart_on_change for the containerd app is limited to patch-level version bumps, and remediation is throttled by a cooldown/backoff policy because restarting the runtime disrupts all running containers.

nodes.label: D-Bus
nodes.rationale: System message bus checked with a dedicated dbus protocol check; watches only alert (no restart remediation) since restarting dbus destabilizes the whole system.

nodes.label: Distributed Checksum Clearinghouse
nodes.rationale: dccifd's pidfile is unreliable across distros (Gentoo observed writing an invalid PID) so the pidfile is optional, and the process check is best-effort because the dccifd identity is not reliably matchable; service state plus the /var/lib/dcc/dccifd socket are the authoritative liveness signals.

nodes.label: DHCP Client
nodes.rationale: Uses a dedicated dhclient protocol check that validates the UDP 68 binding, interface, and lease file freshness.

nodes.label: DHCP Server
nodes.rationale: Per-OS overrides (Gentoo pidfile path, Ubuntu isc-dhcp-server unit and dhcpd user) show the catalog's os: mechanism for distro-specific layout. The dhcp port check is optional since binding depends on configured subnets.

nodes.label: dnsmasq
nodes.rationale: Lightweight DNS forwarder plus DHCP/TFTP server. Restarts on shared-library changes (glibc, systemd-libs, nettle, libidn2) because a long-running resolver keeps stale libraries mapped; remediation is throttled with cooldown/backoff to avoid resolver flapping.

nodes.label: Docker Engine
nodes.rationale: daemon.json is optional, so preflight validates it only when present to let hosts without a config start normally. Config changes use reload (SIGHUP) instead of restart to avoid killing containers, and the engine health uses a docker protocol check on /run/docker.sock; restarts are throttled by cooldown/backoff policy.

nodes.label: Dovecot
nodes.rationale: Plain IMAP (143) and its restart remediation are optional because IMAPS-only hosts do not listen on 143 and must not be flipped to failed or restarted; the cert check on the TLS port (993, 21-day expiry window) is the authoritative TLS health signal. Models the full multi-user process tree (anvil, log, config, stats, auth, imap-login, imap) with distinct dovecot/dovenull/mail users.

nodes.label: etcd
nodes.rationale: Distributed KV store for cluster coordination: generous graceful/term stop timeouts (60s/30s) protect data integrity, kill_only_if guards against killing the wrong process, the /health HTTP check and peer port are optional (peer port depends on cluster membership), and restarts are throttled by cooldown/backoff policy.

nodes.label: Exim
nodes.rationale: SMTP MTA with spool hygiene automation: count checks watch the msglog directory for absolute backlog and fast growth, and interval-scheduled SQLite count queries on the callout/retry hint DBs trigger exim_tidydb cleanup hooks when record limits are exceeded. Cert expiry is watched on the TLS port (465) with a 21-day window.

nodes.label: Fail2ban
nodes.rationale: Reload uses fail2ban-client reload instead of a signal, and liveness uses a dedicated fail2ban protocol check against the server socket. Depends on the python3 app because the server is a Python program, so Python upgrades also trigger a restart.

nodes.label: Fcron
nodes.rationale: The process check is best-effort/optional because the fcron binary path and identity vary by build; service state plus pidfile are the authoritative liveness signals.

nodes.label: Fetchmail
nodes.rationale: Config path is a list (/etc/fetchmailrc or /etc/fetchmail/fetchmailrc) and preflight validates via --configdump only when the file exists, tolerating either layout or absence.

nodes.label: Filebeat
nodes.rationale: Log shipper for Logstash/Elasticsearch: beyond config-syntax preflight, an optional 'test output' command watch verifies the downstream output pipeline is reachable, made optional so a transient collector outage does not fail the local service.

nodes.label: FireHOL
nodes.rationale: One-shot firewall ruleset applier with no long-lived process (processes: {}); effectiveness is verified with a firewall_rules check (auto backend, min_rules 1) gated on the service being active rather than by process liveness.

nodes.label: Exim Spool Hygiene Watches
nodes.rationale: Self-healing mail spool maintenance: msglog file-count watches catch absolute backlog and fast growth (delta within a time window), while interval-scheduled SQLite count checks on the callout/retry hint databases fire exim_tidydb hooks with an age cutoff instead of alerting a human, keeping hint DBs bounded automatically.

nodes.label: firewalld
nodes.rationale: Security-category dynamic firewall daemon; config validated offline via firewalld-offline --check-config before reload, with reload-on-change of /etc/firewalld and a conservative action policy (15m cooldown, max 2 actions/hour, backoff) to avoid restart flapping on a security-critical service.

nodes.label: FreshClam
nodes.rationale: Pidfile is marked optional because its path varies by distro/init (systemd clamav-freshclam vs OpenRC 'freshclam -p /run/freshclam.pid'); the process check is the authoritative liveness signal.

nodes.label: Apache Guacamole (guacd)
nodes.rationale: Includes a restart-if-worker-thread-hot rule (cpu_thread > 90% for 6m triggers restart) because a stuck single-threaded worker degrades remote-desktop sessions; alert-only rules cover the same metric at 5m for visibility.

nodes.label: HAProxy
nodes.rationale: Reload via USR2 signal to the master process for zero-downtime config reload; preflight runs 'haproxy -c -f' to validate config before applying; frontend TCP check is optional+verify since the frontend port may legitimately vary by deployment.

nodes.label: Home Assistant
nodes.rationale: Python application, so restart_on_change tracks the python3 interpreter app version rather than a dedicated binary.

nodes.label: InfluxDB
nodes.rationale: Preflight uses the native 'influxd config validate --config' subcommand to check config.toml before restarts; typed as 'database' service.

nodes.label: Apache Kafka Broker
nodes.rationale: Serves the client data plane (produce/fetch) on the broker listener (port 9092); kafka protocol check expects role=broker and restarts after 3 failed cycles; action policy (cooldown/backoff) limits restart storms on a stateful queue.

nodes.label: Apache Kafka Controller
nodes.rationale: Maintains the KRaft metadata quorum on the controller listener (port 9093); kafka protocol check expects role=controller, mirroring the broker definition but split into a separate service so each listener/role is monitored independently.

nodes.label: KeyDB
nodes.rationale: Health is probed with the redis check type (KeyDB is Redis-protocol compatible) and asserts rdb_last_bgsave_status=ok so persistence failures surface; hot single thread triggers restart after 6m.

nodes.label: libvirt D-Bus
nodes.rationale: D-Bus bridge exposing libvirt objects to desktop and management clients; restarted when the dbus health check fails for 3 cycles.

nodes.label: libvirt (libvirtd)
nodes.rationale: Uses a native libvirt API health check with restart after 3 failed cycles, guarded by an action policy (15m cooldown, max 2/hour, backoff) since restarting the hypervisor daemon is disruptive.

nodes.label: LM Sensors
nodes.rationale: Oneshot-style hardware sensor initialization service: 'processes: {}' declares it has no long-running process, and health is verified by running 'sensors -A' as an optional command check.

nodes.label: Grafana Loki
nodes.rationale: Config verified with 'loki -verify-config' before applying; reload via HUP signal on config change; readiness probed at /ready expecting HTTP 200.

nodes.label: LVM
nodes.rationale: Minimal definition: 'processes: {}' marks it as having no persistent process; only the service-active check applies.

nodes.label: MariaDB Backup Restart Guard
nodes.rationale: Guard rule blocks restart actions while a backup process (mariadb-dump, mysqldump, mariadb-backup, xtrabackup, wal-g) is running as the backup user, to avoid corrupting in-flight database backups.

nodes.label: Monit Service
nodes.rationale: Monit's HTTP interface on port 2812 is opt-in; many hosts run monit without it, so the tcp port check is marked optional so a closed port does not flip an otherwise-active service to failed.

nodes.label: MySQL Backup Restart Guard
nodes.rationale: Guard rule blocks restart actions while a backup process (mysqldump, mysqlpump, mysqlbackup, xtrabackup, wal-g) is running as the backup user, to avoid corrupting in-flight database backups.

nodes.label: From-file Variable Extraction
nodes.rationale: Nebula's lighthouse host and port variables are extracted at runtime from the instance config file via regex patterns over static_host_map, with defaults (127.0.0.1:4242), so per-instance templated services need no hardcoded endpoints.

nodes.label: NFS Client Tracking Daemon Service
nodes.rationale: nfsdcld is socket-activated and short-lived, so the process may legitimately be absent while the unit is active; the process check is optional and the service check is authoritative.

nodes.label: Samba NMB Service
nodes.rationale: Preflight testparm output analysis treats 'lock/pid directory does not exist' messages as ok-severity artifacts so harmless environment warnings do not fail config validation.

nodes.label: OpenVPN Client Service
nodes.rationale: Instanced systemd template (openvpn-client@${instance}); reads listen port from the instance config file with default 1194; port check is optional since clients may not listen locally.

nodes.label: OpenVPN Service (OpenRC)
nodes.rationale: OpenRC variant of the OpenVPN family (openvpn.${instance}) for non-systemd hosts, complementing the systemd client/server template units.

nodes.label: Patroni
nodes.rationale: HA controller for PostgreSQL clusters; long graceful_timeout (60s) and kill_only_if guard (user postgres, patroni binary) protect database failover safety; preflight validates config with --validate-config --ignore-listen-port.

nodes.label: PHP-FPM
nodes.rationale: Versioned/instanced appserver (php-fpm%v%s%i) with many systemd/openrc unit name aliases across distros. The top-level pidfile: already generates a service-gated optional pidfile health check, so a separate watches.pidfile is deliberately omitted to avoid collision. Reload via USR2; kill_only_if restricts kills to the fpm binary run as www-data or root.

nodes.label: PM2
nodes.rationale: Node.js process manager; liveness verified via 'pm2 ping' both as preflight and as a restart-if-ping-failed watch (3 cycles), with backoff policy to avoid restart storms.

nodes.label: PCP Collector (pmcd)
nodes.rationale: Performance Co-Pilot metric collector; tracks multiple PMDA agent processes (pmdaroot, pmdaproc, pmdaxfs, pmdalinux, pmdakvm) and restarts on library changes (glibc, systemd-libs, lzma) rather than app version changes.

nodes.label: PCP Inference Engine (pmie)
nodes.rationale: Process check is best-effort (optional, requires service): after a PCP package update the running pmie's exe reads as '(deleted)' and cannot match by exact exe — a deliberate kill-safety rule — so service + pidfile remain the authoritative liveness signals.

nodes.label: PCP Inference Engine Farm
nodes.rationale: The active unit runs a shell wrapper (the farm loop), not the pmie_farm binary itself, so an exact-exe process match cannot see it; the process check is kept optional as a best-effort signal rather than a hard failure that flips the service.

nodes.label: PCP Archive Logger Farm
nodes.rationale: Process check is optional and matches exe_any of pmpause or pmsleep because the long-lived pmpause may show as pmsleep '(deleted)' after PCP upgrades.

nodes.label: Polkit
nodes.rationale: PolicyKit authorization service health is probed via a dbus check (restart after 3 failed cycles), since polkit is only useful when reachable over D-Bus.

nodes.label: Postfix
nodes.rationale: MTA watched via SMTP protocol check and TCP port (restart after 3 failed cycles) plus an optional TLS certificate expiry check (21 days) on port 465; config validated with 'postfix check' and reloaded via 'postfix reload' on main.cf/master.cf changes.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Versioned service (postgres-%v) with per-OS data/config dir overrides (Debian/Ubuntu use /etc/postgresql, Gentoo /etc/postgresql-${version}); long stop timeouts (graceful 120s, term 60s) and kill_only_if guard protect data integrity; readiness via a dedicated postgres check plus TCP port.

nodes.label: Block Restart During Backup (guard rule)
nodes.rationale: Guard rule that blocks restart actions while the 'backup' watch detects a running backup tool (pg_basebackup, pg_dump, pg_dumpall, pgbackrest, wal-g) under the backup user, so automated remediation never interrupts an in-flight database backup.

nodes.label: PPP Daemon (pppd)
nodes.rationale: PPPoE/dial-up uplink monitored end-to-end along the connectivity chain: service -> link state -> IP address present -> default route -> ICMP probe through the ppp interface -> DNS resolution via resolvconf; restart storms limited by cooldown/backoff policy.

nodes.label: ProFTPD
nodes.rationale: FTP server verified at three levels: service state, TCP port 21, and an FTP protocol check; config validated pre-restart with --configtest.

nodes.label: Prometheus
nodes.rationale: Monitoring server validated with promtool ('promtool check config') before restart and hot-reloaded via SIGHUP when prometheus.yml or rules dirs change; health probed with a dedicated prometheus check type.

nodes.label: QEMU Guest Agent
nodes.rationale: Guest agent liveness approximated by running '${qemu_ga_binary} --version' as a command check (restart after 3 failed cycles) since the agent has no network endpoint to probe.

nodes.label: NFS Mount Daemon Service
nodes.rationale: The mountd RPC port is commonly dynamic, so the standalone daemon monitors init state only; a fixed-port mountd probe is added per service when the host pins a port. The mountd check here is marked optional for that reason.

nodes.label: RPC pipefs Service
nodes.rationale: rpc-pipefs is a mount helper, not a long-running daemon: processes is declared empty and only the init-state (service) watch applies.

nodes.label: Rspamd Service
nodes.rationale: Uses preflight 'rspamadm configtest' so a bad config never reaches a restart, and reload via SIGHUP instead of full restart. Root main process plus unprivileged rspamd worker processes are supervised separately.

nodes.label: Rsyslog Service
nodes.rationale: Preflight validates config with 'rsyslogd -N1 -f <config>' before any restart. Per-OS variable override: runs as user 'syslog' generally but 'root' on Gentoo.

nodes.label: OpenLDAP slapd Service
nodes.rationale: Preflight slaptest wrapper picks -F (config dir) vs -f (config file) at runtime because distros split between /etc/ldap and /etc/openldap layouts. Also watches LDAPS certificate expiry (21 days) on port 636.

nodes.label: S.M.A.R.T. Daemon Service
nodes.rationale: Per-OS service-name override: Ubuntu ships the unit as 'smartmontools' instead of 'smartd'.

nodes.label: Samba SMB/NMB Combined Service
nodes.rationale: Combined unit supervising smbd, nmbd and conditionally winbindd (enabled only if daemon_list in /etc/conf.d/samba contains winbindd). Preflight testparm analysis downgrades 'lock/pid directory does not exist' to severity ok because those directories are runtime artifacts, not config errors.

nodes.label: Samba SMB (smbd) Service
nodes.rationale: Standalone smbd unit for hosts that split Samba daemons. Reload uses 'smbcontrol smbd reload-config' rather than a service restart; same testparm preflight with the dir-artifact downgrade rule as the combined smb unit.

nodes.label: Tomcat AJP CPing/CPong Health Check
nodes.rationale: AJP13 CPing/CPong proves the AJP connector answers, not only HTTP; marked optional because many installs disable AJP and terminate TLS at a reverse proxy. The ajp_port is extracted from server.xml via regex and falls back to 8009 when absent.

nodes.label: virtlockd Plain Socket Probe
nodes.rationale: virtlockd's socket is the lock-manager transport, not a libvirt hypervisor RPC endpoint, so it is probed as a plain 'socket' check rather than the 'libvirt' check type (which virtnetworkd does use).

nodes.label: from_file Variable Extraction Pattern
nodes.rationale: Catalog variables can be resolved at runtime by regex-matching a config file (from_file + pattern + default): upsdrv/upsdrv-instance derive the NUT driver name and instance list from /etc/nut/ups.conf; tomcat derives HTTP and AJP ports from server.xml. This keeps templated multi-instance service definitions self-configuring.

nodes.label: xinetd
nodes.rationale: xinetd's pidfile/exe identity is not reliably matchable across builds (it may run without a pidfile), so the process check is best-effort optional and the service check is authoritative.

nodes.label: Zigbee2MQTT
nodes.rationale: Runs on Node.js, so it links the node app and adds a remediation rule restarting when the node binary path changes.

nodes.label: sermo-all.yml annotated reference bundle
nodes.rationale: Every configuration surface in one validated file: the test suite (internal/config) validates it so it cannot drift from the schema. Reference bundle only; real deployments keep one target per file.

nodes.label: Document kind determined by location
nodes.rationale: A document's kind is derived from the directory it lives in; a top-level kind: key is optional and redundant, but when present must match the location, which catches files placed in the wrong directory. One YAML file per target keeps generated config easy to diff, replace and clean up.

nodes.label: paths configuration block
nodes.rationale: paths.runtime (tmpfs, wiped on reboot) holds locks and op slots; paths.state (persistent SQLite) holds monitor state, SLA, windows and metrics so restarts do not reset remediation windows or dashboards. paths.locks is intentionally unsupported.

nodes.label: Notifiers (email/slack/teams/tty/wall)
nodes.rationale: Named, typed delivery targets referenced from then.notify; global notify default with per-site override; notify: none makes a deliberate monitor-only watch; tty/wall are native Go utmp/TTY writers, no external wall/write command.

nodes.label: Availability (SLA) tracking
nodes.rationale: Only observed cycles count: periods where Sermo is stopped or the service is paused/disabled are excluded rather than counted as downtime, so maintenance windows and Sermo outages never depress a service's SLA; unmonitored minutes are gaps, not 0%.

nodes.label: /readyz readiness probe
nodes.rationale: Returns 200 only after startup_delay and every monitored target's first cycle so the daemon actually has data rather than merely having launched; the fleet's first cycle is staggered to avoid a startup stampede, and a config reload never re-gates readiness.

nodes.label: App variable prefixing
nodes.rationale: App variables are exposed to linking services with a normalized app-name prefix (${cupsd_binary}) so a service can reuse binary paths owned by several apps without collisions; with exactly one linked app the unprefixed names are also exposed as defaults; local variables still win for host overrides.

nodes.label: version_match binary identity matcher
nodes.rationale: Proves the identity of a compatibility binary before considering a catalog app installed — lets MariaDB use an older /usr/sbin/mysqld fallback without also showing the MySQL catalog app on MariaDB hosts; a failed match marks the app not installed even when the binary exists.

nodes.label: Operation engine
nodes.rationale: Manual (sermoctl) and automatic (sermod) actions run through one engine; cooldown gates the decision to act in rule evaluation, not the engine, which is how both share the engine while only automatic remediation is rate limited. Exactly two deferred steps (emit event, release lock) guarantee no exit path leaks the lock or skips its event. A residual Sermo cannot identify is reported, not killed.

nodes.label: Named runtime locks
nodes.rationale: JSON lock files under <runtime>/locks acquired with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and fsync; owner_start_ticks (field 22 of /proc/pid/stat) distinguishes a stale lock from a live one after PID reuse; stale locks are reclaimed with logging, live locks never silently overwritten.

nodes.label: Internal operation lock
nodes.rationale: Serializes start/stop/restart/reload/resume per service; deliberately outside the named-lock namespace so it cannot collide with a user lock named op, is never listed, and cannot be released by sermoctl lock release. A live holder fails fast with exit 75 — the engine never waits or queues.

nodes.label: Scheduler and concurrency model
nodes.rationale: Per-service workers with independent tickers so a multi-minute restart never blocks other services; overlapping ticks are skipped, not queued, avoiding catch-up backlogs; operations and checks use separate global pools; shutdown never force-kills a partially stopped service.

nodes.label: Catalog service (uses:)
nodes.rationale: A reusable base definition; a configured service uses: it and overrides only what differs. High-impact catalog services (databases, caches, queues) carry stricter local policy with longer cooldowns and backoff to avoid restart loops.

nodes.label: restart_on_change (app/library version restarts)
nodes.rationale: Restart a service when a linked app's version or a library changes so long-running processes pick up upgraded binaries instead of running stale code.

nodes.label: Operation pipeline (preflight · guard · locks)
nodes.rationale: Strict order in Engine.Do/Engine.run: acquire per-service oplock, check named runtime locks, run preflight, evaluate guards, only then invoke the init manager, then postflight; every exit path emits the result event via defer.

nodes.label: Lock state classification (classify)
nodes.rationale: Fixed order: TTL expiry, then owner liveness (kill(pid,0)), then PID-reuse detection comparing /proc/pid/stat start ticks; only active locks block actions, expired/stale locks are reclaimable. ProcessProber abstracts /proc access.

nodes.label: Catalog resolution (Load → applyOSSelectors → Resolve)
nodes.rationale: Three stages: Load registers all documents, applyOSSelectors collapses os: blocks by detected OS (SERMO_OS → /etc/os-release → linux), Resolve merges defaults + catalog + user override and expands variables/sections into a flat Resolved.Tree consumed by the init manager, checks, rules and process discovery.

nodes.label: Worker cycle (RunCycle)
nodes.rationale: Per tick: sample metrics, run checks + gates, record SLA/health, publish to web, run remediation (update windows → guard → policy → operate/cascade), run alerts, persist state; the first cycle after start/reload is observation-only.

nodes.label: watchPanels registry (watch-panels.json)
nodes.rationale: Static IDs, columns, controls and copy live in internal/web/src/watch-panels.json shared by the Go shell builder and the runtime registry, so rendering, deep links, attention navigation and search iterate one source of truth.

nodes.label: Canonical wizard question flow
nodes.rationale: One question flow for all assistants so the same mistakes are not repeated: detection drives target identity (never name typing), shared Prompt helpers only, batch answers when several targets, preview before write, and cleanup only offers files whose target is no longer detected.

nodes.label: servicemgr.DetectProcInfo (PID detection)
nodes.rationale: Derives pidfile, executable, cmdline and user from the init definition (systemctl show on systemd; init script + conf.d parsing on OpenRC), best-effort; detected /var/run paths are normalized to canonical /run before storage.

nodes.label: chooseNotifiers helper
nodes.rationale: none and default are always selectable even with zero notifiers configured so the notifier question can never dead-end; default degrades to monitor-only (notify: [none]) with a one-line note when there is nothing to inherit — it never re-asks or aborts. The logic lives once in internal/assist/notify.go.

nodes.label: custom-tool example app
nodes.rationale: Host-specific helper app example that services may link with apps: [custom-tool]; declares a binary preflight and an optional version command.

nodes.label: mount-backup example mount unit
nodes.rationale: fstab-backed storage watch with a mount: block: capacity check (used_pct >= 90%, mounted: true), refcounted mount/umount, and a restrictive kill_only_if (users: backup, exe_any: rsync) for blocker signalling.

nodes.label: ping-gw example network watch
nodes.rationale: icmp watch with per-metric actions: a state-change hook and a latency-threshold hook, showing the metrics: {state, latency} watch form.

nodes.label: Sermo Dev Configuration
nodes.rationale: Exists so repository examples can be validated and inspected without installing under /etc/sermo; builds with SERMO_DATADIR=$PWD, resolves paths relative to examples/, and keeps runtime/state under /tmp/sermo-dev to stay out of /run and /var/lib.

nodes.label: Sermo Installed Configuration
nodes.rationale: Minimal installed config pointing at /etc/sermo and /usr/share/sermo. Runtime data goes on tmpfs (/run/sermo, wiped on reboot) while state lives in /var/lib/sermo so monitor:previous, dashboard readings and remediation cooldowns survive sermod restarts. Web UI only activates when web.port is defined; defaults.policy.cooldown is a required loop-prevention cooldown inherited by every service.

nodes.label: Monitor-Disabled Shipped Examples
nodes.rationale: Shipped watch/network/storage/mount examples use monitor: disabled so copying them cannot immediately run hooks or send notifications; operators must adapt thresholds and set monitor: enabled or monitor: previous per host.

nodes.label: apache-main Service Instance
nodes.rationale: Overrides the engine interval to 15s so the http health-check firing window (for: 5 cycles before restart) counts faster cycles.

nodes.label: mail-queue Service Instance
nodes.rationale: Postfix instance carrying its own watches: deferred-queue backlog count, runaway worker process_count, and hot cpu_thread metric. Service watches are for hooks/notifications tied to service-local signals; remediations belong in rules.

nodes.label: Service-Scoped Process Checks
nodes.rationale: Inside a service, process_count and metric checks are scoped to the service's PID tree (parent plus descendants), so fork storms trip them while unrelated host processes are never counted. Host-scoped net/icmp/swap and the kill-capable process watch are deliberately unavailable in service scope and must be declared in a global watches document. Per-watch metric collectors never disturb the engine's own sampling.

nodes.label: mariadb-backup-guard Service Instance
nodes.rationale: App-linked override representing mariadb-backup as an app plus a guard rule that blocks restart/stop while the backup process is active. Base mysql/mariadb catalog services already have a conservative backup process check; this shape is for hosts needing a different binary/user or explicit app representation. dry_run supports gradual rollout without executing operations.

nodes.label: mariadb-main Service Instance
nodes.rationale: Inherits the mariadb catalog service's unit candidates, service/tcp/ping checks and remediation rules; only overrides the port variable.

nodes.label: mariadb-replica Service Instance
nodes.rationale: sql checks (read_only flag must stay 1; replication lag < 30s) encode deployment-specific policy — query, threshold, credentials — so they belong on an instance, not the mariadb catalog service. Credentials use a read-only monitor user with the password resolved from the environment via ${env:SERMO_DB_MONITOR_PASS}.

nodes.label: mysql-wal-g-backup-guard Service Instance
nodes.rationale: App-linked override for WAL-G MySQL backups: optional process watch for the wal-g binary plus a guard rule blocking restart/stop while the WAL-G backup runs.

nodes.label: nginx-site Service Instance
nodes.rationale: Adds instance-level checks on top of everything inherited from the nginx catalog service: on-disk TLS cert expiry (complements the catalog live-endpoint cert check; a missing/unreadable cert file IS an alert here, which is why the path lives on the instance), restart on sustained high memory (within 15 cycles, 5 matches), and alert on high file descriptors.

nodes.label: Instance-Scoped Deployment Checks
nodes.rationale: Deployment-specific thresholds, certificate paths, per-device targets and credentialed queries belong on service instances rather than bundled catalog services, because baking host-specific values into the catalog would false-alarm on other hosts.

nodes.label: php-fpm-www Service
nodes.rationale: Self-contained (no catalog service) because the bundled php-fpm catalog service is a version template (php-fpm%v) that only materializes when that PHP version is installed; monitoring the unit directly keeps the example version-agnostic. Uses a binary preflight, a master process watch, and restart-if-inactive after 3 cycles.

nodes.label: redis-cache Service Instance
nodes.rationale: A distinct cache instance cloned from redis-main, running as its own unit (service: redis-cache) with port 6380 and its own pidfile.

nodes.label: Clone Before Variable Expansion
nodes.rationale: Cloning copies the source service BEFORE variable expansion, so overriding a single variable like port is enough — every check referencing ${port} resolves to the new value after expansion.

nodes.label: smartd-disks Service Instance
nodes.rationale: smart checks are per-device, so they live on an instance (the smartd catalog service cannot know the host's drives). They read smartctl -j (needs smartmontools + root), poll hourly because SMART rarely changes, and complement smartd's own mail alerts with failure-prediction predicates (reallocated sectors, SSD wear, temperature) that Sermo records and graphs over time.

nodes.label: webapp Self-Contained HTTP Service
nodes.rationale: Self-contained service with no catalog backing: monitors any HTTP health endpoint and restarts the named init unit (service: my-webapp) after 3 failed cycles.

nodes.label: storage-root Root Filesystem Watch
nodes.rationale: Storage watch on / firing a hook when usage reaches 90% for 3 cycles and verifying the mount is present.

nodes.label: clock-drift Host Watch
nodes.rationale: Alerts when wall-clock drift versus NTP servers (time.cloudflare.com, pool.ntp.org) exceeds policy (max_offset 2s, max_stratum 4, max_root_dispersion 250ms); the hook owns correction, not the watch.

nodes.label: conntrack Network Watch
nodes.rationale: Watches the netfilter conntrack table because a full table drops new connections; fires a hook at >=90% used for 3 cycles.

nodes.label: diskio Storage Watch
nodes.rationale: Block-device I/O rates from /proc/diskstats; stateful — needs >=2 cycles to establish a baseline, first cycle never fires. device: takes a kernel device name (sda, nvme0n1), not a /dev path.

nodes.label: edac Watch (ECC Memory Errors)
nodes.rationale: Uses the kernel EDAC subsystem (no device, no root) so it is portable on ECC hosts. Uncorrectable errors (ue > 0) are always serious; correctable errors (ce) are tolerated up to a noise-floor threshold of 100.

nodes.label: Hook Alert Action (then.hook)
nodes.rationale: Standard action pattern across example watches: on check failure run an external alert script (/usr/local/bin/sermo-*-alert.sh) via then.hook.command, keeping the daemon decoupled from the notification transport.

nodes.label: entropy Watch (Kernel Entropy Pool)
nodes.rationale: Low entropy stalls crypto / TLS; alerts when avail < 200 for 3 consecutive cycles.

nodes.label: For-Cycles Debounce (for: cycles)
nodes.rationale: Watches require N consecutive failing cycles before firing (for: { cycles: N }) to suppress transient spikes and alert flapping.

nodes.label: fds Watch (System File Descriptors)
nodes.rationale: Watches system file descriptor usage against the kernel fs.file-max limit; alerts at used_pct >= 85 for 3 cycles.

nodes.label: incoming-files-fresh Watch (File Age)
nodes.rationale: check type file with older_than: 24h over multiple paths; alerts once per path when a file has not been modified within the expected age. Summary template interpolates ${value}, ${older_than}, ${number_files}.

nodes.label: Notify Action (then.notify)
nodes.rationale: Alternative to hooks: route alerts to configured notifiers (then.notify: [name]), optionally gated by notify_on transitions such as on_change, on_degraded, on_good.

nodes.label: firewall-rules Watch
nodes.rationale: Verifies nftables/iptables still has rules loaded (backend: auto, min_rules: 1); useful to catch a firewall loader that silently flushed rules.

nodes.label: hdparm Watch (Disk Throughput Benchmark)
nodes.rationale: Per-device buffered-read benchmark via `hdparm -t/-T` (needs hdparm + root). Polled only every 12h because it runs a real disk benchmark; copy the file once per disk and set device: before enabling.

nodes.label: load Watch (Load Average)
nodes.rationale: per_cpu: true normalizes load5/load15 thresholds per core so the same thresholds are machine-agnostic.

nodes.label: lvm-vg0-root Watch (LVM / Thin Pool Health)
nodes.rationale: Read-only LVM health and thin-pool capacity (thin_data_pct / thin_metadata_pct >= 80%); absence, partial or suspended volumes make the check unhealthy.

nodes.label: mem-pressure Watch (Kernel PSI Memory)
nodes.rationale: Watches kernel PSI (% of wall time tasks stalled waiting on memory, some_avg60 > 10) because the kernel's own pressure signal catches thrashing that load and memory watches can miss.

nodes.label: memory Watch (RAM via MemAvailable)
nodes.rationale: Uses the kernel's MemAvailable estimate (used_pct >= 90%). Ships with dry_run: true so events are emitted without executing hook/notify actions during hook rollout.

nodes.label: Dry Run Mode (dry_run: true)
nodes.rationale: During hook rollout, dry_run emits events but does not execute hook or non-console notify actions — a safe staging mode for new remediation. Also the default in remotely generated install configs.

nodes.label: oom Watch (OOM Kills)
nodes.rationale: With no delta predicate the check fires on any OOM kill (> 0).

nodes.label: pid-table Watch (kernel.pid_max)
nodes.rationale: Watches threads vs kernel.pid_max (used_pct >= 90) because a full PID table makes every fork()/clone() fail host-wide.

nodes.label: kill-stale-sudo Watch (Process Kill Policy)
nodes.rationale: Stale-privileged-session hygiene: terminate any root-owned /usr/bin/sudo alive longer than 120 minutes. Shipped disabled and must be enabled deliberately because it signals real processes and the daemon must run as root.

nodes.label: Native Kill Action (then.kill)
nodes.rationale: then.kill is native (no external script): it reuses the daemon's own process signaller — the same kill(2) path used by service-stop and mount blocker signalling. Safety constraints: requires an absolute resolved /proc/<pid>/exe name path and a user, so it cannot kill by basename alone; supports TERM->KILL escalation with term_timeout/kill_timeout.

nodes.label: raid Watch (Linux md RAID Health)
nodes.rationale: Reads /proc/mdstat (no device, no root), portable on any host with md arrays. degraded > 0 fires on any degraded array; optional recovering predicate tracks resync windows. A per-array variant supports sysfs_changes: true, raid_control pause_resume and transition-based notify_on.

nodes.label: sensors Watch (hwmon / lm_sensors)
nodes.rationale: Hardware temperature/fan/voltage via hwmon, targeting a chip + label discovered with `sensors`. No root required; thresholds must be adjusted to the hardware before enabling.

nodes.label: smart Watch (Drive SMART Health)
nodes.rationale: Daily `smartctl -H -A -j` per device (needs smartmontools + root). With no predicates it alerts only on the overall SMART FAILED verdict; reallocated/wear/temperature predicates give earlier warning. This is the standalone host-watch variant; a per-drive list tied to the smartd service lives in examples/services/smartd-disks.yml.

nodes.label: swap Watch (Usage + Paging IO)
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates the multi-metric `metrics:` block: one check (type swap) drives two independent alert conditions with separate hooks — usage.used_pct >= 80 and io.delta > 1000 pages swapped per cycle (thrashing).

nodes.label: zombies Watch (Zombie Processes)
nodes.rationale: Accumulating zombies (count > 20) indicate a parent not reaping its children.

nodes.label: Dashboard HTML Source Template
nodes.rationale: Source version of the dashboard shell with a /*__SERMO_CSS__*/ placeholder inside the nonce'd <style> tag; the build inlines the compiled CSS to produce internal/web/index.html.

nodes.label: CSP Nonce Injection ({{CSP_NONCE}})
nodes.rationale: The inline <style> carries nonce="{{CSP_NONCE}}", substituted per-response by the server so a strict Content-Security-Policy can allow only the daemon's own inline styles.

nodes.label: Remote Deployment Workflow
nodes.rationale: Scripts are intentionally small wrappers around Sermo's own binaries: stage read-only host inventory, generate one-file-per-target config, apply under /etc/sermo, start sermod, verify the Web UI. Mutating remote scripts must run as root on the target.

nodes.label: prepare_payload.sh
nodes.rationale: Builds the deployment payload from a local build (GOAMD64=v1, SERMO_DATADIR=/usr/share/sermo). Payload tarballs are written with numeric root:root ownership so local workstation ownership is never preserved onto system paths.

nodes.label: generate_install_config.py
nodes.rationale: Generates one-file-per-target config from staged inventory. Defaults: monitor only installed catalog services with active init units, dry_run: true, Web UI on 0.0.0.0:9797, storage free-space < 5% with 5G expansion, SMART 24h, hdparm 6h, LVM and logged-in-user checks disabled. Adds per-md-array raid watches from staged /proc/mdstat, safe storage checks for every local non-pseudo filesystem, NFS endpoint checks for fstab nfs entries, an alert-only clock drift watch (time.cloudflare.com / pool.ntp.org, > 3s over two samples), and a GeoIP file-age watch (older_than: 480h) when /usr/share/GeoIP exists. Uses endpoint hints to override catalog variables.host/port/user and disables profile endpoint watches lacking a matching listening socket, recording reasons in config-report.json.

nodes.label: remote_stage.sh
nodes.rationale: Installs the payload, replaces stale packaged catalog files, writes a minimal /etc/sermo/sermo.yml, and collects read-only host inventory used by config generation.

nodes.label: remote_apply.sh
nodes.rationale: Replaces generated config directories under /etc/sermo, validates the config, enables/restarts sermod, and verifies the local Web UI.

nodes.label: remote_update_payload.sh
nodes.rationale: Refreshes binaries/catalog on an already configured host, validates /etc/sermo with the detected init backend, restarts sermod and verifies the Web UI. HTTP probes bounded to 5s (SERMO_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). Cleans only its exact /tmp work directory and uploaded payload on success; failed updates keep artifacts for diagnosis (SERMO_KEEP_REMOTE_ARTIFACTS=1 retains them on success too).

nodes.label: remote_update_binary_catalog.sh
nodes.rationale: Refreshes only sermoctl, sermod and the packaged catalog. Snapshots /etc/sermo, rejects payloads containing any other path, and rolls back binaries and catalog if validation, restart or authenticated Web UI checks fail.

nodes.label: remote_normalize_retired_umount_keys.sh
nodes.rationale: Removes only the retired mount.umount.allow_lazy: false and allow_sigkill: false keys from existing YAML; rejects non-false values, validates with the candidate binary and restores /etc/sermo if validation fails.

nodes.label: remote_update_network_watches.sh
nodes.rationale: Refreshes only /etc/sermo/networks from a generated payload; rejects any other archive member, validates, restarts sermod, and restores prior network watches on validation or restart failure.

nodes.label: remote_repair_catalog.sh
nodes.rationale: Replaces only the packaged catalog from a payload.

nodes.label: remote_final_check.sh
nodes.rationale: Validates /etc/sermo, service state, port 9797, /livez, /readyz, the HTML shell and current protected-path metadata.

nodes.label: collect_endpoint_hints.sh
nodes.rationale: Collects sanitized endpoint hints (service config files, listening sockets) from already installed hosts without replacing /etc/sermo; hints feed variables.host/port/user overrides in config generation.

nodes.label: collect_runtime_targets.sh
nodes.rationale: Collects Docker containers and libvirt/QEMU domains from already installed hosts without replacing /etc/sermo.

nodes.label: Protected Path Metadata Guard
nodes.rationale: Extracting archive entries for protected parent directories (/, /etc, /usr, /etc/systemd, /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d, ...) as root can rewrite host metadata. Payloads use numeric root:root ownership, remote extraction uses tar --no-same-owner, and each mutating remote script records protected_path_metadata.before/.after/.diff and exits with status 70 if any protected path changes type, mode, uid or gid.

nodes.label: First-Four-Host Gate (Fleet Failure Handling)
nodes.rationale: The pause-after-four-hosts gate applies only to workflows that mutate remote Sermo state (install, update, apply config, start daemon). Read-only inventory/event collection sweeps the whole fleet in one pass. Unreachable or locally-broken hosts are recorded and skipped, never forced through; the fleet stops only for a reproducible Sermo blocker (defective binary/catalog/config/script, invalid artifact, or protected-path metadata change), which must be fixed and validated locally before redeploying touched hosts.

nodes.label: Default Alert Notification Template
nodes.rationale: Passthrough notification template: subject and body are just {{ .Subject }} / {{ .Body }}, preserving Sermo's built-in formatting while providing the file users copy to customize notifications.
